# Authenticate as standard_user without inheriting administrative-only access

> Prove that a standard user can authenticate into the normal full-access banking experience without receiving administrative-only view, data, or capabilities.

## Step 1

Open https://qaplayground.com/bank/login in a fresh browser session and store the visible unauthenticated login page state as baseline_login_state.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-28

On the QA Playground Bank Demo login page at https://qaplayground.com/bank/login, sign in with username standard_user and password bank_sauce, then assert the session leaves the unauthenticated login state and shows the normal/full-access banking experience represented by standard_user.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-24

From the authenticated standard_user landing/dashboard and its visible banking navigation, inspect the role-specific content available in the session, then assert no administrative view, administrative data, or administrative-only capability is exposed.

content.title: Authenticate as admin_user into the administrative banking experience
content.test_md_blob:
# Authenticate as admin_user into the administrative banking experience

> Prove that admin_user authentication lands in the intended administrative experience and exposes admin-distinct information or controls plus authorized administrative capabilities or data.

## Step 1

Open https://qaplayground.com/bank/login in a fresh browser session and store the visible unauthenticated login page state as baseline_login_state.

## Step 2 @verifies ac-25

On the QA Playground Bank Demo login page at https://qaplayground.com/bank/login, sign in with username admin_user and password admin_sauce, then assert the session leaves the unauthenticated login state and reaches the administrative experience for admin_user.

## Step 3 @verifies ac-26, ac-27

From the authenticated admin_user landing/dashboard and its visible banking navigation, inspect the role-specific content exposed to the session, then assert at least one administrative capability or administrative data point is visible and the information or controls are distinguishable from ordinary customer-facing banking information.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Highest value because it is the negative auth-boundary path: if standard_user can inherit admin-only access, the role-separation promise fails directly and privileged exposure reaches ordinary users.

[value_score] High value because it proves the intended admin-user success path and the presence of admin-specific authorized content, which is the positive half of the role split promised by the source.

[self_critique] The written check proves the state-transition promise in ac-28 by capturing the login-state baseline before authentication. I kept the admin-exclusion assertion on the visible authenticated experience only, which matches the owner-approved login/session scope and avoids over-broad claims about undocumented direct routes.

[self_critique] The test separates the admin transition proof from the admin-content proof so the oracle for ac-25 does not silently stand in for ac-26 or ac-27. I did not add a second negative admin-route test because the corpus does not name a route and the owner scoped this round to documented login/session behavior.

[self_critique] A negative case was not missing: sc-9 covers the standard-user exclusion path, while sc-10 covers the positive admin landing path. The remaining limitation is specificity of the admin marker; the source promises admin-distinct view/data/capabilities at PRD level but does not enumerate a named admin-only control.
